clinical_review.procedure: Reviewed independently by a medical expert and by a project author. No knowledge base was accepted until every critical item was approved or explicitly flagged for revision. Review was divided by clinical condition.
medical_expert_checklist: The disease-specific diagnostic framework is clinically appropriate.
All concepts are correctly classified as diagnostic, supportive, etiologic, severity, complication, or exclusion evidence.
Every diagnostic rule, criterion, threshold, unit, timing condition, and population restriction is confirmed.
No unsupported rule was invented, and supportive findings cannot independently confirm the diagnosis.
The what-does-not-count, contradiction, insufficient-evidence, abstention, and referral rules reflect safe clinical practice.
Every clinical item is accurately grounded in the cited sources.
project_author_checklist: All concepts and rules have correct source provenance.
The JSON structure, concept identifiers, rule references, and value types are valid and consistent.
Missing evidence remains unknown and cannot accidentally activate a rule.
The verifier is deterministic and reports the decision, supporting evidence, missing or conflicting evidence, and justification.
Clear positive, unsupported, incomplete, contradictory, and threshold-boundary cases are tested.

all_knowledge_bases: A claim-by-claim audit was introduced. Every diagnostic concept, threshold, and relationship was required to trace to one of the two cited sources. Derived elements, such as language normalization and differential-handling logic, were relabelled as implementation logic rather than guideline facts.

Each concept was assigned one of four states: present, absent, unknown, or conflicting. Missing documentation remains unknown. Diagnostic, supportive, etiologic, severity, complication, and management evidence are stored separately, so that only explicitly diagnostic evidence can activate the verifier.

The four knowledge bases keep different decision structures rather than one shared formula: a two-of-three rule for pancreatitis, integrated clinical and imaging assessment for cholecystitis, CT-supported multi-evidence assessment for diverticulitis, and stepwise risk stratification followed by imaging for appendicitis.

Unsupported or partially supported claims were deleted or rewritten, and explicit cautions were added stating that no official two-of-three rule exists for appendicitis, cholecystitis, or diverticulitis.
diverticulitis: The Lameris combination of left-lower-quadrant tenderness, CRP above 50 mg/L, and absence of vomiting was retained only as supportive triage evidence, not as a replacement for CT confirmation.
The unsupported statement that CRP rises within 24 hours was replaced with the WSES-supported description that CRP may be delayed by 6 to 8 hours and peaks at approximately 48 hours.

clinical_review.known_limitation: Each condition carries one clinician's assessment, so criterion-level agreement between clinicians is not available. Specialty-matched review by two independent clinicians per condition, with adjudication of disagreement, precedes clinical use.
clinical_review.record_of_review: Supplementary Material, section 4 (expert review and acceptance checklist) and Table S1 (specific improvements introduced during iterative revision).

disease.scope: diagnostic and severity-staging KB for suspected acute left-sided colonic diverticulitis (ALCD) in clinical notes, labs, and imaging reports

sources.title: 2020 update of the WSES guidelines for the management of acute colonic diverticulitis in the emergency setting

scientific_guardrails.rationale: WSES 2020 diverticulitis does NOT define a 2-of-3 or similar n-of-m diagnostic rule. WSES suggests assessing suspected ALCD using clinical history + signs + laboratory inflammatory markers + radiological findings, and explicitly suggests against diagnosis based only on clinical examination.
diagnosis_should_not_be_based_on: LLQ pain alone without imaging or labs
low CRP alone to exclude very early disease (WSES notes CRP may not have risen early)
must_report_uncertainty_when: CRP is low but symptom onset is very acute, because WSES notes a 6–8 h delay from onset and peak at 48 h

features overlap with source-listed differentials such as acute appendicitis, mesenteric ischemia, pelvic inflammatory disease, ovarian cyst, ectopic pregnancy, pyelonephritis, IBS/irritable bowel disease, pancreatitis, cholecystitis, or cholangitis

logic: Suspected ALCD should be assessed using clinical history + signs + laboratory inflammatory markers + radiological findings.
Diagnosis based only on clinical examination is discouraged.
Contrast-enhanced CT scan of the abdomen is the first-choice imaging technique in suspected ALCD.
Ultrasound by an expert operator can be used initially; CT after inconclusive/negative US is a safe stepwise approach.
Patients with CRP >150 mg/L should always undergo CT.

The Lameris 3-feature rule (direct tenderness only in the LLQ + CRP >50 mg/L + absence of vomiting) identified a high-probability clinical subgroup in the cited study; for this KB, imaging is still required before assigning a research-grade confirmed label.
primary_rule.evidence_grade: multiple weak-to-strong recommendations; CT first-choice imaging is weak/moderate (2B); against clinical-exam-only diagnosis is weak/very-low (2D)

symptoms.display: change in bowel habits (constipation or diarrhea)

synonyms: direct tenderness in left lower quadrant

physical_exam.display: direct tenderness ONLY in left lower quadrant (no other quadrant)
physical_exam.exact_quote: direct tenderness only in the left lower quadrant

temporal_features.display: CRP may not have risen yet in very acute-onset disease; WSES notes a 6–8 h delay from onset and peak at 48 h

general.diagnostic_use: supportive; also severity stratification; not alone confirmatory
supportive inflammatory marker; WBC >12,000 cells/mm³ is one SIRS/admission index in StatPearls

thresholds.meaning: One of three Lameris-rule features (with LLQ-only tenderness and absence of vomiting); supports high clinical probability of ALCD but does not replace imaging.
thresholds.exact_quote: (1) direct tenderness only in the left lower quadrant, (2) CRP > 50 mg/l, and (3) absence of vomiting

thresholds.meaning: Independent risk factor for acute complicated diverticulitis; WSES recommends patients with CRP higher than 150 mg/L always undergo CT examination.
thresholds.exact_quote: a CRP value over 150 mg/l and old age were independent risk factors for acute complicated diverticulitis

thresholds.meaning: Optimal threshold reported in WSES-cited studies discriminating severe/complicated from mild/uncomplicated disease (PPV 36%, NPV 92%, sensitivity 61%, specificity 82%); not a standalone diagnostic criterion.
thresholds.exact_quote: The optimal threshold was reached at 175 mg/l with a positive predictive value of 36%, negative predictive value of 92%, sensitivity of 61%, and specificity of 82%

thresholds.meaning: One of the systemic inflammatory response/admission indexes listed by StatPearls; not a diverticulitis-specific diagnostic threshold.

normal_lab_caution.statement: Do not rule out diverticulitis solely because CRP is low in very acute-onset disease; WSES notes a 6–8 h delay from onset and CRP peak at 48 h.

pathway_policy.statement: In patients with suspected ALCD, contrast-enhanced CT scan of the abdomen is the imaging technique of first choice.
pathway_policy.exact_quote: In patients with suspected ALCD, we suggest contrast-enhanced CT scan of the abdomen ... as the imaging technique of first choice

pathway_policy.statement: US may be used in the initial evaluation of patients with suspected ALCD when performed by an expert operator; CT after inconclusive or negative US is a safe approach.
Patients with CRP higher than 150 mg/L should always undergo CT examination.
Assess renal function before IV contrast.

ct_findings.display: pericolic fat stranding / increased pericolic fat density
extraluminal gas / pericolic air bubbles / distant free gas

us_findings.display: US may be used initially by an expert operator in suspected ALCD
us_findings.caution: US summary sensitivity/specificity 90%/90% vs CT 95%/96%; US is operator-dependent and has limitations in obese patients, free gas, and deeply located abscesses.

complicated_findings: fistula (StatPearls complication/imaging sign; not part of WSES CT stage 0–4 definitions)
normalization_notes.caution: Stage assignment requires CT — see WSES CT-guided classification.

severity_assessment.primary_classification: WSES CT-guided classification (2015 WSES Acute Diverticulitis Working Group)

stages.criteria: Diverticula, thickening of the wall, increased density of the pericolic fat
stages.exact_quote: 0 Uncomplicated diverticulitis. Diverticula, thickening of the wall, increased density of the pericolic fat

stages.criteria: Pericolic air bubbles or small amount of pericolic fluid without abscess (within 5 cm from inflamed bowel segment)
stages.exact_quote: 1A Pericolic air bubbles or small amount of pericolic fluid without abscess (within 5 cm from inflammed bowel segment)

stages.criteria: Distant gas (> 5 cm from inflamed bowel segment)
stages.exact_quote: 2B Distant gas (> 5 cm from inflammed bowel segment)

stages.criteria: Diffuse fluid without distant free gas
stages.exact_quote: 3 Diffuse fluid without distant free gas

stages.criteria: Diffuse fluid with distant free gas
stages.exact_quote: 4 Diffuse fluid with distant free gas

severity_assessment.note_on_typo_in_source: The WSES 2020 PDF contains the spelling "inflammed" rather than "inflamed" in stage 1A and 2B descriptions; this KB preserves the source quote verbatim in exact_quote fields and uses the standard spelling "inflamed" elsewhere.
severity_assessment.note_on_complementary_classifications: Hinchey, modified Hinchey (Kaiser 2005), Neff, Mora Lopez classifications also exist; WSES 2020 does not recommend any one classification as superior. This KB defaults to WSES CT-guided classification for research-grade structured output.

differential_diagnosis.source_policy: Differential guardrails are restricted to differential diagnoses explicitly listed in the StatPearls text or directly discussed in WSES; detailed distinguishing clues are treated as implementation prompts only when source-grounded.

overlap: abdominal/lower abdominal pain; right-sided diverticulitis may present similarly to appendicitis
distinguishing_clues: site of diverticulitis affects presentation; imaging/clinical evaluation needed
items.agent_action: Consider because StatPearls explicitly lists acute appendicitis and notes right-colon diverticulitis may present similarly.

distinguishing_clues: not specified in the source text
items.agent_action: Consider as a source-listed differential; do not invent additional discriminators unless present in case evidence.

distinguishing_clues: pregnancy test in females of childbearing age is explicitly recommended to rule out ectopic pregnancy
items.agent_action: Consider source-listed gynecologic differentials; use pregnancy test context when relevant.

distinguishing_clues: not specified in the source text
items.agent_action: Consider as a source-listed differential; do not overcall diverticulitis when urinary evidence dominates.

overlap: change in bowel habits and abdominal pain
distinguishing_clues: StatPearls notes diverticulitis presentation may be confused with IBS; it also lists irritable bowel disease/syndrome in the differential list.
items.agent_action: Consider when bowel-habit symptoms dominate without imaging/lab support for diverticulitis.

overlap: abdominal pain; transverse colon diverticulitis may appear as upper-abdominal disorders
distinguishing_clues: site-dependent presentation noted by StatPearls; no additional discriminators encoded.
items.agent_action: Consider as source-listed differentials, especially when pain localization is not LLQ.

distinguishing_clues: WSES discusses risk of malignancy after CT-proven diverticulitis and notes abscess can mimic malignancy.
items.agent_action: Use only as follow-up/alternative concern where supported; do not infer cancer from LLQ pain alone.

differential_diagnosis.notes: Note: WSES 2020 covers left-sided colonic diverticulitis. Right-sided diverticulitis can mimic appendicitis and is more common in Asian populations.

input_schema.symptoms: list of extracted symptoms with evidence text and negation
input_schema.physical_exam: list of signs with evidence text and negation
input_schema.labs: structured WBC, CRP, temperature if available
input_schema.imaging: structured CT/US findings with modality and report text
input_schema.timeline: hours/days from symptom onset if available

decision_algorithm.name: Clinical extraction
decision_algorithm.logic: Extract LLQ pain/tenderness, fever, bowel habit change, vomiting status, peritoneal signs.

decision_algorithm.name: Lameris rule check
decision_algorithm.logic: If LLQ-only tenderness + CRP >50 + absence of vomiting are all true, flag as high clinical probability per WSES.

decision_algorithm.name: CRP-driven imaging triage
decision_algorithm.logic: If CRP >150, mark mandatory CT per WSES.

decision_algorithm.name: Apply CT findings to WSES classification
decision_algorithm.logic: When CT is available, map WSES-classifiable findings to stage 0, 1A, 1B, 2A, 2B, 3, or 4; keep non-WSES complications such as fistula separate from WSES stage assignment.

decision_algorithm.name: Confirm or defer
decision_algorithm.logic: Confirm only when imaging supports diverticulitis with consistent clinical context; otherwise label suspected/needs_imaging.

decision_algorithm.name: Complication & red flag check
decision_algorithm.logic: Flag abscess, fistula, peritonitis, sepsis, free air.

abstention_rules: If only LLQ pain is documented without imaging or labs, do NOT confirm — label suspected_diverticulitis_needs_imaging.
If Lameris rule is fully met but imaging is absent, label high_clinical_probability_imaging_pending — do NOT label confirmed for research-grade output.
If CRP is low in very acute-onset disease, do NOT exclude diverticulitis based on CRP alone because WSES notes delayed CRP rise and peak at 48 h.

If imaging shows WSES-classifiable complicated findings (pericolic air/fluid, abscess, distant gas, diffuse fluid with/without distant free gas), assign the appropriate WSES CT stage; if imaging shows fistula, mark complicated disease but do not force it into a WSES 0–4 stage.
Do NOT invent a 2-of-3 diagnostic rule for diverticulitis — WSES does not provide one.

forbidden_outputs: confirmed diverticulitis from clinical exam alone
exclusion of diverticulitis based only on low CRP in very early presentation

evidence_interpretation_layer.purpose: Convert extracted features into conservative diagnostic support patterns for the LLM agent.
global_rules: For this KB, do not assign a research-grade confirmed diverticulitis label without imaging support; WSES discourages diagnosis based only on clinical examination and recommends complete assessment including radiological findings.
Map CT findings to WSES CT-guided classification (0, 1A, 1B, 2A, 2B, 3, 4) when available.

CRP thresholds have different source-grounded meanings: >50 mg/L is part of the Lameris rule; >150 mg/L is associated with complicated disease risk and CT recommendation; 175 mg/L is an optimal threshold reported in a cited study for discriminating complicated vs uncomplicated disease.
When evidence conflicts, preserve both directions and lower confidence.

patterns.confirmation_requirement: CT imaging support required for research-grade confirmed label.
Implementation policy: even with all 3 Lameris features, this KB requires imaging before a research-grade confirmed label because WSES recommends complete assessment including radiological findings.
patterns.caution: In the original Lameris study, 29 of 30 patients with all 3 features had ALCD — but 1 did not. Research-grade label still benefits from imaging.

patterns.action_for_agent: Assign specific WSES stage based on dominant feature: 1A (air bubbles/small fluid within 5cm), 1B (abscess ≤4cm), 2A (abscess >4cm), 2B (distant gas >5cm), 3 (diffuse fluid no gas), 4 (diffuse fluid with gas).
Flag CT requirement/recommendation per WSES for CRP higher than 150 mg/L.
Flag possible complicated disease/peritonitis context and preserve urgency; CT/staging still depends on imaging findings when available.

contradictory_and_uncertainty_layer.purpose: Prevent LLM overdiagnosis by representing negative, conflicting, or alternative-direction evidence.

contradictory_or_confidence_lowering_fea.meaning: Right-colon diverticulitis may present similarly to acute appendicitis; right-sided diverticulitis has different epidemiology.
Consider source-listed bowel differentials such as irritable bowel syndrome/irritable bowel disease or mesenteric ischemia when case evidence does not support ALCD.

Consider source-listed gynecologic differentials such as pelvic inflammatory disease, ovarian cyst, or ectopic pregnancy; pregnancy test is recommended in females of childbearing age with abdominal pain.
Do not rule out diverticulitis only because CRP is low in very acute-onset disease; WSES notes delayed CRP rise and peak at 48 h.
Diverticula without wall thickening or stranding do not support acute diverticulitis.

Consider malignancy mainly as a follow-up/alternative concern in source-supported contexts such as complicated diverticulitis or abscess; WSES discusses malignancy risk after CT-proven diverticulitis.

required_agent_behavior: Report contradictory or alternative-direction evidence in the output.
State what evidence would move the case from suspected to imaging_confirmed.
Never silently drop normal labs or negative imaging.
Always assign a WSES CT stage when CT findings are available.

clinical_nlp_context_layer.purpose: Make extraction safer by tracking negation, temporality, and experiencer per feature.

temporal_interpretation_rules.rule: CRP has a delay of 6–8 h from onset and reaches peak at 48 h; low CRP in very acute-onset disease should not be used alone to exclude ALCD.
Diverticulitis is described as an acute presentation; chronic or non-acute features should be treated as lower-confidence for current acute ALCD unless imaging/labs support it.
After acute episode resolution, StatPearls recommends colonoscopy 6 to 8 weeks later, particularly if the patient has not had colonoscopy in the past 2 to 3 years.

negation_examples.note: Negation of vomiting IS positive for Lameris rule.

source_grounded_exclusions.excluded_claim: Diverticulitis has an official 2-of-3 diagnostic rule.
source_grounded_exclusions.reason: Not supported by WSES 2020. WSES recommends complete assessment using clinical history, signs, inflammatory markers, and radiological findings; Lameris is a 3-feature clinical rule, not an official 2-of-3 diagnostic rule.
source_grounded_exclusions.replacement: Use multi-evidence assessment framework; CT confirms.

source_grounded_exclusions.excluded_claim: CRP alone can confirm or exclude ALCD.
source_grounded_exclusions.reason: WSES 2020: CRP supports severity prediction and is part of Lameris rule but is not standalone diagnostic.
source_grounded_exclusions.replacement: Use CRP as severity triage / Lameris rule component, not as sole rule-in/rule-out.
Use complete assessment; for this KB, require imaging support for research-grade confirmed output.

source_grounded_exclusions.excluded_claim: WSES Hinchey stage 1B and modified Hinchey stage 1B mean the same thing.
source_grounded_exclusions.reason: Multiple classifications exist (Hinchey, modified Hinchey/Kaiser 2005, Neff, Mora Lopez, WSES). They differ in substages and thresholds.
source_grounded_exclusions.replacement: Always state which classification is being used; default to WSES CT-guided classification for research output.

source_audit.summary: Claim-by-claim verification found the WSES CT classification, Lameris criteria, CRP thresholds, CT/US pathway, and many StatPearls presentation/complication claims source-grounded. Several interpretive, temporal, and differential-diagnosis details were narrowed, relabeled as inference, or rewritten to match the source documents only.
cautions: This KB is for research LLM diagnostic support only.
WSES 2020 does not provide an official 2-of-3 diagnostic rule for diverticulitis; the Lameris rule has 3 features and is a clinical probability rule reported in WSES.
CT-guided staging requires CT imaging; do not stage from clinical features alone.
WSES 2020 covers left-sided ALCD primarily; right-sided diverticulitis has different epidemiology.

strict_audit_outputs.external_knowledge_policy: No outside clinical knowledge retained unless explicitly relabeled as implementation policy or reasonable inference from the source documents.
hallucinations_or_unsupported_claims: General symptom fever threshold >38°C was unsupported in symptom context; moved/limited to SIRS/admission context.
CRP <24h cutoff was unsupported; replaced with WSES 6–8 h delay and 48 h peak wording.
Specific US finding “thickened colonic wall with diverticula on US” was not clearly traceable; rewritten as US expert-operator pathway.

Detailed differential clues such as migratory pain, vascular risk factors, bloody diarrhea, renal colic to groin, epiploic appendagitis CT features were not supported by the source documents and were removed.
Fistula was incorrectly grouped with WSES CT stage assignment; retained as StatPearls-supported complicated disease but separated from WSES stage 0–4 mapping.
weak_provenance_areas: Differential diagnosis: StatPearls gives a list but limited distinguishing clues; keep discriminators conservative.
Clinical NLP temporal rules: sources support acute presentation and CRP kinetics, not detailed chronicity rules.
Research-grade confirmation policy: conservative implementation derived from WSES complete-assessment guidance, not a verbatim guideline rule.
partially_supported_claims: Lameris high-probability rule supports a clinical subgroup, but imaging-confirmation requirement is KB policy derived from WSES framework.
Alternative-more-likely pattern is a reasonable inference, not an explicit WSES diagnostic exclusion rule.
Colonoscopy/neoplasm language should follow source-specific contexts rather than broad cancer-mimic assumptions.
